newsitem.title: EGYPT: First Egyptian BMW rolls off assembly line.
newsitem.headline: First Egyptian BMW rolls off assembly line.

text.p: The first BMW car put together at the German car maker's only Middle Eastern plant on Wednesday rolled off the assembly line located just outside the Egyptian capital Cairo.
Bernd Pischetsrieder, chairman of the board of Bayerische Motoren Werke, drove the 523i model car off the assembly line at the Sixth of October City plant which began production in May.

"BMW's philosophy is that we want to be in the markets we regard as important. Egypt is important particularly for imports so the second logical step was to set up a CKD (completely knocked down) plant," Pischetsrieder told Reuters.

He said the assembly plant is BMW's ninth in the world and has an initial capacity of 2,500 cars per year. BMW invested more than 60 million German marks ($35 million) in the project, which will be run by local assembly partner Al Fotouh Company for Vehicle Assembling (ACVA).

The only line currently in operation produces the luxury five-series model but Houssam Aboul Fotouh, chairman of ACVA, said the firm was planning to introduce a three-series production line maybe by next year.
The Egyptian government imposes crippling duties on imported cars but makes tariff reductions on CKDs if at least 40 percent of the car is made using locally made components.
ACVA say the Egyptian 523i will be sold for 286,000 pounds ($84,000), much less than the 400,000 pounds a customer pays for the German import.

BMW said it sold 322 cars in Egypt last year, up from 263 sold in 1995. The German firm estimates the total car market to increase in a few years to 100,000 units a year from its current 60,000 units and the luxury car segement to almost double to 13,000 units.
